technique: Exclusive <details name> laid out as tabs
notes: HTML has no native tabs element, and the ARIA tabs pattern (tablist, arrow-key focus, aria-selected) needs JavaScript. So this version does not pretend to be one: it is a group of `<details>` sharing a name, which the browser keeps exclusive. Each `<summary>` is a real button with an expanded state, sits right before its own content in the DOM, and works with Tab, Enter and Space.

The tab look is pure layout. Each `<details>` is set to `display: contents` so every `<summary>` joins one grid row, and its `::details-content` slot is placed in the row below. Browsers without `::details-content` keep a plain accordion, which is fully usable.

Honest trade-offs: screen readers announce disclosure buttons, not tabs; arrow keys do not move between tabs; and a keyboard user can collapse the active tab (mouse clicks on it are ignored). Compared to 2014's hidden radios, whose labels were not focusable at all, it is a real improvement, but a fully spec-compliant tabs widget still needs a few lines of script.
